about: What a data team can find in the logistics records, scored against the answer key. Generated by scripts/analysis/logistics.py from public/data/india-grocery.

generic.name: Shipments: arrival after dispatch, a 30-minute slot
generic.sql: SELECT * FROM shipments WHERE arrived_ts <= dispatched_ts OR slot_end - slot_start <> INTERVAL 30 MINUTE

generic.name: Shipping notice: shipment, pallet and line are unique
generic.sql: SELECT shipment_id, sscc, line, count(*) AS n FROM notice_lines GROUP BY ALL HAVING count(*) > 1

generic.name: Shipping notice: every item and barcode is in the product master, units are cases times the case size
generic.sql: SELECT n.* FROM notice_lines n LEFT JOIN products p ON p.sku = n.sku AND p.gtin = n.gtin WHERE p.sku IS NULL OR n.units <> n.cases * p.case_units

generic.name: Pick confirmations: one per notice line, same order, item and cases, confirmed by a scan
generic.sql: SELECT n.*, p.cases_confirmed FROM notice_lines n LEFT JOIN picks p USING (shipment_id, line) WHERE p.sku IS NULL OR p.sku <> n.sku OR p.order_id <> n.order_id OR p.cases_confirmed <> n.cases OR p.confirmed_by IS NULL OR p.cases_confirmed > p.cases_ordered

generic.name: Pallets: every pallet on a notice is in the pallet table, with the same tare on every pallet
generic.sql: WITH w AS (SELECT n.sscc, sum(n.cases * p.case_kg) AS cases_kg FROM notice_lines n JOIN products p USING (sku) GROUP BY n.sscc), t AS (SELECT round(pl.notice_kg - w.cases_kg, 1) AS tare FROM w LEFT JOIN pallets pl USING (sscc)) SELECT tare, count(*) AS pallets FROM t GROUP BY tare HAVING (SELECT count(DISTINCT tare) FROM t) <> 1 OR tare IS NULL

generic.name: Goods receipts: every notice line booked, as its shipping notice says
generic.sql: SELECT n.*, r.sku_booked, r.units_booked FROM notice_lines n LEFT JOIN goods_receipts r USING (shipment_id, sscc, line) WHERE r.grn_id IS NULL OR r.asn_sku <> n.sku OR r.asn_units <> n.units OR r.sku_booked <> r.asn_sku OR r.units_booked <> r.asn_units

generic.name: Goods receipts: booked when the truck arrived
generic.sql: SELECT r.* FROM goods_receipts r JOIN shipments s USING (shipment_id) WHERE r.received_ts <> s.arrived_ts

generic.name: Store orders: every order line is on the next morning's shipping notice
generic.sql: SELECT o.* FROM store_orders o LEFT JOIN notice_lines n ON n.order_id = o.order_id AND n.sku = o.sku WHERE n.sku IS NULL AND CAST(o.created_ts AS DATE) < (SELECT max(CAST(arrived_ts AS DATE)) FROM shipments)

generic.name: Warehouse adjustments: units are cases times the case size, value is units at cost
generic.sql: SELECT a.* FROM dc_adjustments a JOIN products p USING (sku) WHERE a.units <> a.cases * p.case_units OR abs(a.value_at_cost_inr - a.units * p.cost_inr) > 0.01

generic.name: Store counts: each adjustment is the count minus the book
generic.sql: SELECT * FROM stock_counts WHERE adjustment <> counted - book_before

views.v_corrections: every count correction in both buildings, in units and in cases
views.v_mirror_pairs: pairs of corrections in one product family with opposite signs, each at least a case and within 15% of each other in cases, within 7 days: neighbouring slots or one store count, or the same item in both buildings
views.v_receipt_survival: receipt lines whose next count, within a week, took off half or more of what was booked
views.v_otif_by_delivery: OTIF per delivery by the warehouse's picks, by the store's receipts, and reconciled with counts
views.v_censored_hours: 5 kg open hours the gap detector flagged, or with no stock on the books

definitions.SSCC: A serial number for a pallet. It identifies the pallet, not what is on it.
definitions.pick confirmation: A scan of the slot's label. It confirms where the picker stood, not what was picked.
definitions.goods receipt: Booked by scanning the pallet label against the shipping notice. A copy of the notice, not an observation of the cases.
definitions.in full: Every case is what was ordered. Only an independent observation can say so: a case scan, a scale, or a later count.
definitions.count correction: Says the book was wrong, not why.

rules: Pair count corrections before you explain them: equal and opposite in cases, in one family, in neighbouring slots, at one count, or across the two buildings.
Trace a warehouse pair to the picks of the item that came up over, from its slot, in the cases the pair moved, in the week before.
A receipt that does not survive the next count was not what its notice said.
